classification.difficultyReason: Identify an intermediate angle using alternate angles, then use the straight-line relationship to calculate and justify the requested angle.

spec.description: Two rising parallel lines E–P–A and D–Q–B meet descending transversal F–P–Q–C. All three lines have two terminal arrowheads. Named points and single parallel chevrons are retained. The upper sector PQB at Q bears 111 degrees.
spec.mathematics: The printed 111-degree angle gives EPQ=111 degrees by alternate angles, then FPE=69 degrees by a straight angle. The source depicts the labelled upper sector as visually acute; drawing proportions retain that source discrepancy pending review.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied 111-degree angle is printed; no answer annotation is placed at P.

answer.short: $\angle EPQ=111^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines). $\angle FPE=69^\circ$ because it and $\angle EPQ$ form a straight angle.
answer.worked:
$\angle EPQ=111^\circ$ (alternate angles on parallel lines).

$$\begin{align*}\angle FPE+\angle EPQ&=180^\circ\\\angle FPE+111^\circ&=180^\circ\\\angle FPE&=69^\circ\end{align*}$$
Angles on a straight line.
